title: Methodological workflow for assessing heterogeneity in immature organic-rich carbonate reservoirs
author: Aljurf, Abu-Mahfouz, et al.

steps.title: Acquire and prepare core samples
steps.instruction: Obtain a vertical core by drilling, slab the core for observation, collect representative samples every 50 cm (and additionally across visually identifiable lithological boundaries), prepare ~30 µm thin sections for each lithofacies and chemofacies, and core plugs of 1‑inch diameter for porosity and ultrasonic velocity measurements.

substeps.instruction: Drill and retrieve vertical core from target formation
Slab core surfaces for visual observation
Collect representative samples at regular 50 cm intervals and at lithological boundaries
Prepare ~30 µm thin sections for each lithofacies and chemofacies
Core plug preparation: 1‑inch diameter plugs for porosity and velocity tests

steps.title: Non‑destructive high‑resolution characterization
steps.instruction: Perform a suite of non‑destructive measurements on the entire core interval to generate continuous, high‑resolution datasets of lithology, petrophysics, and mechanics.

substeps.instruction: Describe lithology on slab surfaces using visual observation and a 10× hand lens; classify lithofacies with the Dunham carbonate classification system; examine ~30 µm thin sections for mineral composition, textures, fossils, and diagenesis

Acquire continuous petrophysical data with a Multi‑Sensor Core Logger (MSCL): bulk density, compressional‑wave velocity (Vp), and magnetic susceptibility (MS) at 5 cm intervals; perform spectral gamma‑ray (SGR) analysis to quantify uranium, thorium, potassium and obtain the SGR curve
Measure rock hardness with a Proceq Equotip Bambino2 micro‑rebound tester; record Leeb Hardness every 5 cm and calibrate each measurement with a D‑block reference standard

Calculate the mineral‑based brittleness index (MBI) using the equation MBI_GR = Qz + Carb Qz + Carb + Clay + TOC, where Qz = quartz %, Carb = carbonate % (Ca % + Mg %), Clay = clay %, TOC = total organic carbon %

Perform scratch testing on slab surfaces with an Epslog Wombat device to obtain Intrinsic Specific Energy (ISE) profiles; translate ISE values to unconfined compressive strength (UCS) to generate a continuous strength log

steps.title: Identify chemofacies via multivariate analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze the continuous high‑resolution dataset with multivariate statistical techniques to objectively classify chemofacies.

substeps.instruction: Apply Principal Component Analysis (PCA) to reduce dataset dimensionality and reveal dominant geochemical trends
Conduct Hierarchical Clustering on Principal Components (HCPC) to group samples into clusters with similar geochemical signatures
Assign each cluster as a chemofacies representing distinct mineralogical composition, organic‑matter content, depositional conditions, and diagenetic alteration

steps.title: Destructive laboratory analyses
steps.instruction: Select representative samples from each lithofacies and chemofacies and carry out targeted destructive tests to quantify mineralogy, chemistry, organic content, porosity, and elastic properties.

substeps.instruction: Collect powdered samples <50 µm at vertical intervals of at least 50 cm (additional samples across lithological boundaries); use powders for mineral and organic analyses
Determine mineral composition by X‑ray diffraction (XRD)
Analyze major and trace elements by X‑ray fluorescence (XRF)

Run Rock‑Eval 7S pyrolysis on 30–50 mg of powder in an inert nitrogen atmosphere: isothermal hold at 300 °C for S1 (free hydrocarbons), then heat to 650 °C at 25 °C min⁻¹ to obtain S2 (residual hydrocarbons), S3 (CO₂), Tmax (temperature of S2 peak), and record TOC, hydrogen index (HI), sulfur content (TS), S1‑S3
Measure porosity on 1‑inch diameter core plugs using a HEP‑P Helium porosimeter

Measure ultrasonic velocities on 1‑inch plugs at ambient pressure with a NER Autolab benchtop velocity device; convert travel times to compressional (Vp) and shear (Vs) velocities using plug length, then calculate dynamic Young’s modulus and Poisson’s ratio

steps.title: Integrate data and model heterogeneity
steps.instruction: Depth‑match all continuous petrophysical/mechanical logs with discrete laboratory results in a single database, correlate these datasets with the lithofacies and chemofacies classifications, and interpret intervals where facies transitions coincide with changes in measured properties as heterogeneous zones; use the integrated dataset for predictive modeling of reservoir heterogeneity.
